response.explanation: OrderNotificationService sits in the notifications application layer. Its sendConfirmation method should only format and send a confirmation email. Instead it works out the order's pricing itself: line 9 applies a 10% discount when the order has more than three lines, and line 10 subtracts that discount from the subtotal to get the payable amount. This is a pricing/discount business rule, and the agreed fact puts its natural layer in the domain. The rule flags it because the logic lives in an application service of a different bounded context (notifications) and not in the ordering domain, for example on the Order aggregate next to Order.subtotal(), which the graph shows the service already calls. As a result the discount policy is hidden in a notification path. Other consumers such as invoicing or checkout cannot reuse it, and it can drift from them. No project docs, ADRs or comments were provided that say anything about where this logic belongs, and none grant an exception.
